claims.wording: The listing's MacCare - Mac Cleaner is MacCare at getmaccare.com, attributed to Martin Wiederhold.
MacCare advertises macOS 14+, Intel and Apple Silicon support.
claims.conditions: No hardware/runtime tests; not Windows support

claims.wording: MacCare documents eight scan categories, a TreeMap, app-remnant uninstaller and startup-item management.
claims.excerpt: Scans 8 junk categories in parallel: caches, logs, temp files, app remnants, duplicates, downloads, mail attachments, system junk.
additionalExcerpts: See exactly where your storage went with an interactive TreeMap.
Removes apps along with all their hidden remnants: caches, preferences, containers, launch agents and logs.
Manage Login Items, LaunchAgents and system daemons.
claims.conditions: Not complete-coverage, safe-removal or boot-speed proof

claims.wording: MacCare advertises Audio Producer Mode for DAW-related plugins, libraries, presets and caches.
claims.excerpt: MacCare automatically detects your DAW and protects all audio-related files like plugins, sample libraries, presets and caches.
claims.conditions: Attribute; no tested compatibility or total-protection claim; omit exclusivity assertion

claims.wording: The documented cleanup model includes immediate safe-file cleanup followed by individual suggestions.
claims.excerpt: One scan. Two phases. Safe files are cleaned instantly. Then you review suggestions one by one with previews.
claims.conditions: Not approval for every action; qualify with v1.7.2 notes MC08

claims.wording: MacCare advertises Pro at $29/year with a seven-day trial/cancel-anytime wording, and Lifetime at $69 once with all future updates.
claims.excerpt:

additionalExcerpts:

claims.wording: The homepage download links to the MartinWiederhold maccare-releases v1.7.2 installer; public release metadata confirms that tag.
claims.conditions: Published 2026-07-19T17:43:45Z, draft false, prerelease false. Homepage-linked version, not certified latest. No binary downloaded.

claims.wording: v1.7.2 notes restrict automatic Step 1 to caches, logs and build artifacts in the home folder; other suggestions use per-item Keep/Delete.
claims.excerpt: Safe Cleanup (the one-click Step 1) now has a strict guardrail: it only ever removes caches, logs and build artifacts from your own home folder.
claims.additionalExcerpt: the Trash and Mail attachments are no longer eligible for automatic cleanup. Anything like that only appears in Step 2 (Suggestions), where you decide Keep or Delete per item.
claims.conditions: Media/documents/music excluded according to notes. Not our implementation audit or safety guarantee.

claims.wording: The vendor describes Trash/Put-Back support and a disk-space menu-bar monitor.
claims.excerpt: Every deleted file goes to Trash with full Put-Back support, never permanently removed.
claims.additionalExcerpt: A small, always-visible disk space indicator in your menu bar. One click for a quick scan, plus your last cleanup stats at a glance.
claims.conditions: No tested restoration guarantee; no inference of grouped CPU monitoring or recurring-growth attribution

claims.wording: Vendor says the universal v1.7.2 binary is Apple-notarized.
claims.excerpt: Universal binary (Apple Silicon + Intel). Notarized by Apple.
